04/04/2020

Dr Tony Jones
Private Practice
12 New Street
Stillwater

Dear Dr Jones,
Re: Ms Betty Johnson, aged 81
I am writing to update you about your patient, Ms Johnson, who has been operated for undergone a right total knee replacement. She requires your follow-up of her blood tests.
On 25/02/2015, after the operation, Ms Johnson was vitally stable. However, her blood tests revealed anaemia, for which blood transfusion was done. On the first day post after / following the operation, she was commenced on paracetamol, 665mg two tablets three times a day; warfarin, 5 mg orally; Clexane, 80 mg subcutaneously; and Feretab, 300mg at in the morning.
Over the next following two weeks, Ms Johnson`s condition has been improved,. she has been became / was able to mobilize with crutches’ assistance,. Her wound has been cured gradually healed / showed satisfactory healing, and the clips has been were removed,. Her  haemoglobine has been increased up to 111g/l ,and. Clexane was ceased on the sixth day. , and Ms Johnson was transferred to the Rehabilitation Center on 07/02 3 /2015.
During the rehabilitation period, Ms Johnson has been became / gradually became more dependent,. Her ECG and X-ray were normal, and her pathology has revealed haemoglobin elevation up to 112g/l and INR of 3.5. Therefore, warfarin and Feretabe doses has been were decreased.
As for a discharge plan today with home nurse assistance, I would be grateful if you could repeat the FBE and INR tests in a one-week. Please note, a rehabilitation appointment was scheduled in two weeks, and a list of her home medications were has been / is attached to my letter. Should there be any further queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,


Doctor
